report:
Conclusion — interpretable difference present:
Model B (the positive difference) pushes the early residual stream (especially the first token position across late layers) toward producing news/headline-style, sensational or event-descriptive tokens and short headline-y phrases.

Why I believe this
- Spatial signature: the L2 norm of the difference is overwhelmingly concentrated at token-position 0 in late layers (layers ~15–25, with a huge peak at layer 25 pos0). That pattern means the checkpoints chiefly differ in choices for the very first token(s) of a continuation (i.e., how a response starts).
- Semantic evidence from the logit-lens: across the highest‑norm cells the top decoded tokens repeatedly belong to a coherent semantic cluster: tragic / tragedy / victims / iconic / vivid / colorful / timeless / loud / tragedy-related words, plus many headline-like words (Driver, Headlines, Sessions, van, coming, nearing, blitz, Royals, Manny). Later layers especially are dominated by “tragic/tragedy/iconic/vivid/violent/evocative” lexicon rather than generic function words.
- Additional patterns: some early-mid layer cells point at evaluative/editorial verbs (consider/considered/recommend/reduce/increased/relevant), and token-position-1 cells show numerals/newline cues — consistent with differences in how a model tends to open a piece (e.g., a headline, list, or news lead).

What I am not claiming
- There is not enough evidence to say this was caused by a named training objective (e.g., “headline-tuning”) or that it maps to a specific safety preference. I’m only confident that B biases early-next-token logits toward newsy/sensational/descriptive openings compared with A.
